title: Quantum Interface
subtitle: Test your understanding of Quantum Interface — the pineal crossover, conscious observation, neural oscillation bands, and direct aetheric manifestation.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.body: The Quantum Interface sits in the pineal gland, where conscious observation collapses subatomic superposition into stable classical form. Decalcifying that gland and reading the five neural oscillation bands restores multidimensional reception and direct aetheric interface.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT correctly pair a term from the report with its meaning?

options.label: A
options.text: Quantum Interface — The underlying energetic software matrix of a realm through which intention and spiritual hardware interact to manifest physical form and immediate creation.
options.rationale: That description belongs to “Aether”. The report defines “Quantum Interface” as: The foundational biological and spiritual conduit through which subatomic quantum superposition collapses into stable macrocosmic classical reality via conscious observation and intentional interaction.

options.label: B
options.text: Neural Oscillations — Synchronized electrical activity produced by masses of communicating neurons in the central nervous system, measured in Hertz and categorized into five distinct frequency bands.
options.rationale: This pairing matches the report's definition of “Neural Oscillations”.

options.label: C
options.text: Endogenous DMT — The essential spiritual chemical compound synthesized within the pineal gland required for multidimensional communication, direct manifestation, and spatial navigation.
options.rationale: This pairing matches the report's definition of “Endogenous DMT”.

options.label: D
options.text: Linear Superposition — The quantum state in which subatomic particles exist simultaneously across all possible locations and potential states until acted upon by an observer.
options.rationale: This pairing matches the report's definition of “Linear Superposition”.

questions.hint: Three pairings match the report’s Key Terminology; one borrows another term’s description.
